leads.title: Federal Decree-Law No. 31 of 2021 - Federal Crimes and Penalties Law
leads.documents: Primary law criminalizing consensual same-sex conduct and cross-dressing; complaint requirement and penalties relevant to LGBTQ/trans visitor risk
leads.detail: Cited as Article 409(1)(b) minimum six months' imprisonment, Article 409(5) complaint by spouse or guardian only, Article 412(2) men disguising as women to enter women-only space up to one year + AED 10,000; came into force 2 January 2022; replaces 1987 Federal Penal Code. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: U.S. Department of State - 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: UAE
leads.documents: Institutional government report on criminalization of consensual same-sex conduct and enforcement record
leads.detail: Quoted in text: 'Both civil law and sharia criminalize consensual same-sex sexual conduct between adults. The penalty for individuals who engage in consensual sodomy with a man is a minimum prison sentence of six months if a complaint is filed by the partner or the guardian. There were no known reports of arrests or prosecutions for consensual same-sex sexual conduct.' No URL visible in text.

leads.title: U.S. Department of State annual human rights reports on UAE after 2015
leads.documents: Government reporting series documenting no records of arrests or prosecutions for same-sex sexual activity since at least 2015 (as of 2026)
leads.detail: Cited via Human Dignity Trust summary: all annual reports after 2015 have stated no records of arrests or prosecutions for same-sex sexual activity. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Human Dignity Trust
leads.documents: British non-profit human-rights assessment summarizing US State Department reporting on UAE enforcement history
leads.detail: Cited as: According to the British non-profit, Human Dignity Trust, as of 2020, all annual human rights reports from the U.S. Department of State on UAE after 2015 have stated there are no records of arrests or prosecutions. No URL visible in text.

leads.documents: Government censorship machinery banning film for depicting same-sex relationship as violating media content standards
leads.detail: Cited as June 2022 ban of Pixar's Lightyear in cinemas for violating Emirates' media content standards. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: New York Times - June 2023 Amazon UAE restrictions reporting
leads.documents: Institutional press report documenting state-required blocking of LGBTQ search terms and book listings on Amazon UAE
leads.detail: Cited as: Amazon blocked search results for 150 terms, terms such as lgbtq, pride, and closeted gay return no results, removal of listings e.g. Bad Feminist by Roxane Gay, under threat of penalties. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: The New Arab - May-June 2022 Majid comic investigation reporting
leads.documents: Press report documenting UAE investigation of children's magazine for allegedly promoting homosexuality and withdrawal of edition
leads.detail: Cited as: Majid withdrew May 2022 edition depicting multi-colored character saying Ali will wish to become like me, using Arabic word mithli meaning both homosexual and like me. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: 2017 Abu Dhabi conviction of two Singaporean nationals for attempting to resemble women
leads.documents: Documented cross-dressing/gender-expression enforcement case directly relevant to trans visitor safety: detention, conviction, custodial conditions
leads.detail: Cited as: 9 August 2017 detained in shopping mall, convicted and sentenced to one year in prison for attempting to resemble women, deported 28 August after nearly three weeks in custody including cell said to be designated for effeminate people. No outlet/URL visible in text beyond case facts.
